name: Two π/2 scalars
summary: Two legless π/2 spiders equal the global phase i times 2, written with two-spider scalars.
description:
A legless Z-spider with phase π/2 is the scalar $1+i = \sqrt2 e^{i\pi/4}$. Two of these multiply to $2i$, which can be written as the [scalar](../scalar-state-effect/) $\sqrt2 e^{i\pi/2}$ (a π/2 Z-spider connected to a π X-spider) times √2 (a phase-free pair of spiders).

This is one of the rules that relates the 'odd' Clifford scalars $1\pm i$ to global phases. Note that a single $1+i$ cannot be written with only Clifford two-spider scalars (it has phase π/4), so such legless spiders must be paired up.
